Unresectable tumor localized to certain "favorable" sites (e.g., the orbit) also has a high likelihood of cure.

qs.q: A 4-year-old child presents with a localized rhabdomyosarcoma of the orbit. Based on clinical features affecting prognosis, how is this primary site classified?
qs.e: Orbit and non-parameningeal head and neck sites are classified as favourable. Extremity and parameningeal sites carry an unfavourable prognosis.
qs.s: Rhabdomyosarcoma in Children: Sites, Types and Treatment: MCQs

qs.q: A 13-year-old boy is diagnosed with a localized rhabdomyosarcoma of the thigh. Compared to a tumor of the orbit, how is the prognostic grouping of the thigh tumor classified?
qs.e: Extremity sites are classified as unfavourable, whereas orbital sites are favourable. This distinction significantly impacts survival statistics and treatment intensity.
